 Zach LaVine says the Kings are still looking for an identity 
 That's one problem, to be sure. By Ian Goodwillie | Nov 19, 2026, 7:00 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Nov 10, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Sacramento Kings guard Zach LaVine (8) reacts after scoring during the fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a disastrous 22 and 60 season in 2025-2026, the Sacramento Kings are off to a one and 13 start in 2026-2027. Zach Lavine, in his post-game media time after their most recent loss, said the team still lacks an identity . That may be true, but they're not going to build one the way they play.
--> After a disastrous 22 and 60 season in 2025-2026, the Sacramento Kings are off to a one and 13 start in 2026-2027. Zach Lavine, in his post-game media time after their most recent loss, said the team still lacks an identity . That may be true, but they're not going to build one the way they play.
 To be fair to LaVine, we all know what he means. A team with an identity has a consistent style and approach to everything they do. That means who they are as a group both on and off the court, as well as their offense, defense, culture, development, and everything else that makes a team a team.
--> To be fair to LaVine, we all know what he means. A team with an identity has a consistent style and approach to everything they do. That means who they are as a group both on and off the court, as well as their offense, defense, culture, development, and everything else that makes a team a team.
 Possibly the best example of this is the Miami Heat. They are a culture-first organization with a strong identity that permeates all aspects of the franchise. It's how they took in Davion Mitchell after being cast away by the Kings and helped turn him into one of the best young point guards around .
--> Possibly the best example of this is the Miami Heat. They are a culture-first organization with a strong identity that permeates all aspects of the franchise. It's how they took in Davion Mitchell after being cast away by the Kings and helped turn him into one of the best young point guards around .
 The Kings quite literally have none of that, which is what LaVine is referring to. And he's not wrong. If you had to honestly sit down and define the culture of this franchise, it would be impossible. The only unifying factor the Kings have is losing, and that is definitely not what any team wants as an identity.

If you had to honestly sit down and define the culture of this franchise, it would be impossible. The only unifying factor the Kings have is losing, and that is definitely not what any team wants as an identity.
 A cultural turnaround is due in Sacramento basketball
--> A cultural turnaround is due in Sacramento basketball
 Realistically, building an identity is a long-term goal. The Kings will not be able to do it with a lot of their current pieces in place. Doug Christie will definitely have to go at some point, though it might not be until after this season. It would be exceedingly helpful if Vivek Ranadive was to leave , as well.
--> Realistically, building an identity is a long-term goal. The Kings will not be able to do it with a lot of their current pieces in place. Doug Christie will definitely have to go at some point, though it might not be until after this season. It would be exceedingly helpful if Vivek Ranadive was to leave , as well.
 Yes, that also means the team rebuild has to continue, but the Kings need to get a handle on what they're trying to accomplish. Trading Nique Clifford away was in opposition to the stated goals of the rebuild. Plus, what they got in return for Clifford wasn't as good as what they traded to get him.
--> Yes, that also means the team rebuild has to continue, but the Kings need to get a handle on what they're trying to accomplish. Trading Nique Clifford away was in opposition to the stated goals of the rebuild. Plus, what they got in return for Clifford wasn't as good as what they traded to get him.
 At this point, pretty much everyone has already written this 2026-2027 off as a lost season for the Kings. Based on their current momentum, Sacramento is projected to win six games. Even that feels optimistic. Now, they have to decide what they can do with this time to build for the future.
--> At this point, pretty much everyone has already written this 2026-2027 off as a lost season for the Kings. Based on their current momentum, Sacramento is projected to win six games. Even that feels optimistic. Now, they have to decide what they can do with this time to build for the future.
 That means actually developing rookies and sophomores, not overplaying veterans they know are moving on, and taking their head coach situation seriously. The Kings need to stop waiting for the future and start actually building towards it. Then, they will find an identity as LaVine has suggested.
